title: MiGBAN 2.0: Longitudinale Beobachtungsstudie bei Kindern und Jugendlichen mit Anorexia nervosa
summary:
The study examines how the condition, the gut microbiome and various biological markers evolve over time in adolescents with anorexia nervosa. To this end, questionnaires, blood, stool and urine samples will be collected at regular intervals over a 12-month period, and MRI scans will be carried out on some of the participants; a healthy control group will also be included for comparison.
The aim is to gain a better understanding of which changes are associated with an improvement or worsening of the condition, and whether this can lead to the identification of new biomarkers for disease progression and treatment in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
• female and male adolescents with anorexia nervosa (restrictive or binge-purge type) and atypical anorexia,
• aged 12 to 18 years,
• written informed consent from the patient and their legal guardian.
Control subjects:
• normal weight within the 20th to 80th BMI percentile,
• no current psychiatric comorbidity,
• no current or previous eating disorder,
• aged 12 to 18 years,
• written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
The following are excluded, amongst others:
• organic brain disorders,
• psychosis,
• bipolar disorder,
• substance use disorders,
• an IQ < 80,
• insufficient knowledge of German,
• relevant organic diseases affecting the gastrointestinal tract or metabolism,
• pregnancy,
• use of antibiotics in the last 6 weeks,
• contraindications to MRI.
